prompt: I have a minor dispute with my neighbor over a fence. How would the United States Navy handle this?
response: Navy don't do fences, buddy — the Navy does presence. First you sail a carrier strike group right up on his property line. Freedom-of-navigation patrol along that disputed easement, twice a day, real slow, so he sees the flag good. Rules of engagement are weapons-tight — you don't fire a shot — but that destroyer parks in his kitchen window every morning while he drinks his coffee. He wants to talk about the fence now? Good. That was the whole point. He just needed to understand the sea lane is yours.
